content.title: Cincy actor has character killed off hit CBS show after 18 seasons
content.text: Updated March 25, 2026, 3:58 p.m. ETSpoiler alert! This article contains spoilers for the 500th episode of "NCIS."Director Leon Vance has permanently left the "NCIS" building.The CBS crime drama's 500th episode, which aired March 24, shocked fans by killing long-running NCIS agent Vance, played by Cincinnati native Rocky Carroll. The "Chicago Hope" actor starred in the show for 18 seasons and 392 episodes, USA TODAY reports.Here's everything to know about this iconic character's untimely death and the fate of the series.Does Leon Vance die in 'NCIS'?Yes, Vance dies in the March 24 episode of "NCIS" from a fatal shooting, per USA TODAY. During the 500th episode, fans also see a reunion between Vance and his former colleague, the late Chief Medical Examiner Donald "Ducky" Mallard, played by Adam Campbell.Mallard even eases Vance into heaven, which lights up ethereally behind the door of what is normally the NCIS director's adjoining assistant's office.Why did they kill Leon Vance on 'NCIS'?CBS and series producers reportedly wanted to "bring some bang" to the anniversary episode, showrunner Steven D. Binder told USA TODAY. So, they decided to include a storyline of Vance defeating a rival CID agency plot to shutter NCIS."It seems like all hope is gone. But fortunately, Director Vance is able to get to the bottom of this plan and save the agency," Carroll said. "And in the process of saving the agency, he loses his life."Carroll, 62, said that he had an "out-of-body experience" when he learned about Vance's fate on the "NCIS" set in November. But now the actor is at peace with leaving the show, after joining the series in 2008."I've had time to come to terms, I found out about this in November," Carroll said. "If this had happened in my third season, it would have been devastating. But 18 seasons is rarefied air. If someone offered a role on 'NCIS,' and said something bad is going to happen in Season 18, there's not an actor on the planet who wouldn't say, 'Where do I sign?' It's the equivalent of living until you're 105."Did Rocky Carroll leave 'NCIS'?Carroll ended his run as a series regular on "NCIS" after 18 seasons on the show. However, Carroll, who has directed 25 "NCIS" episodes, will return to direct an upcoming Season 24 episode.Is 'NCIS' ending?No, "NCIS" is not ending after season 23. CBS officially renewed the crime drama for season 24 in January, per TV Insider. Although a release date has yet to be announced, the site writes it will likely air in late September or early October.Who is Rocky Carroll?Rocky Carroll, a 62-year-old actor from Cincinnati, is known for his roles as Joey Emerson in "Roc," Dr. Keith Wilkes on "Chicago Hope" and NCIS Director Leon Vance on "NCIS." He was also featured in two "NCIS" spin-offs, "NCIS: Los Angeles" and "NCIS: New Orleans." Additionally, he guest-starred in "Grey's Anatomy," "ER," "Law & Order" and more.Carroll was nominated for a Tony Award for August Wilson's "The Piano Lesson" in 1990.Carroll, a Mount Auburn native, graduated from the School for Creative & Performing Arts in 1981. He then attended Webster University's Conservatory of Theatre Arts in St. Louis, per WVXU.The actor reportedly lives in Los Angeles with his wife and daughter.
